# silkify

> Turn a picture into a touchable silk object on a web page. At rest it is matte and photographic; where the pointer touches it, the surface dents, ripples and shines like satin. Use when someone wants to "silkify" a logo, product shot, fruit, animal, portrait, painting, the moon or any other image, or asks for a silk, satin or fabric ripple-on-hover effect, or wants an interactive WebGL hero object made from a PNG. Covers cutting the subject out, inflating its silhouette into a dome, choosing a material and feel (satin, velvet, wet, foil, paper, ink; water, gel, jelly), tuning it live in the Lab, and embedding the three.js renderer in plain HTML or React.

silkify is a WebGL library (one ES module on three.js) plus an Agent Skill. To use it, copy its src/ folder into the project, install three.js there, and import silk.js by its path (an import map names three for a plain page; a bundler needs nothing). The CDN is the alternative for a page with nowhere to put files.

An agent installs the skill by following this instruction: Install the silkify agent skill: git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.2.3 https://github.com/RussGuo/silkify into a folder named silkify in the directory you load skills from (~/.claude/skills for Claude Code; ~/.agents/skills for Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI and most other agents), then read its SKILL.md and tell me whether silkify is ready.

## Skill

- [SKILL.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RussGuo/silkify/v0.2.3/SKILL.md): the steps an agent follows: get the code, cut out the subject, choose puff, material and feel, render in HTML or React, verify
- [Parameters](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RussGuo/silkify/v0.2.3/references/parameters.md): every option with its default and tuning range, the material and feel presets, recipes from the gallery
- [Performance](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RussGuo/silkify/v0.2.3/references/performance.md): device tiers, when the loop sleeps, many objects on one page, what breeze and autoplay cost, measurements
- [Troubleshooting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RussGuo/silkify/v0.2.3/references/troubleshooting.md): symptom, cause and fix: halos, creases, black squares, no ripple, the worker falling back

## Use

- [src/](https://github.com/RussGuo/silkify/tree/v0.2.3/src): the library, the folder to copy into the project (silk.js is the entry point)
- [Lab](https://russguo.github.io/silkify/examples/lab.html): every option as a live control; prints the options to copy
- [Gallery](https://russguo.github.io/silkify/examples/): ten objects with the options that make each look right

## Alternative: the CDN, for a page with nowhere to put files

- [silk.js on jsDelivr](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/RussGuo/silkify@v0.2.3/src/silk.js): the entry point, pinned to the release tag; the rest of src/ loads from beside it, and the page then depends on jsDelivr
- [Minimal CDN page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RussGuo/silkify/v0.2.3/examples/cdn.html): the smallest page that uses the CDN way

## Integrations

- [Cursor rule](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RussGuo/silkify/v0.2.3/integrations/cursor/silkify.mdc): for .cursor/rules/
- [Copilot instructions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RussGuo/silkify/v0.2.3/integrations/copilot/silkify.instructions.md): for .github/instructions/ (applies to page and component files only)
